reason: Local-only table for the time-card OCR feature; live apply is a separate, deliberate step (scripts/time-card-schema.sql), not yet done.
Django-era live columns are varchar(n); the test schema uses text. Same values accepted for this app's data (length limits are not hit in practice).
Django-era live ids/FKs are bigint; the test schema uses integer. Range difference is irrelevant at this data volume.

Django-era live columns are NOT NULL without a DB default (Django supplies values in the ORM); the test schema adds defaults. Local is more lenient here, so tests must still send explicit values for fields the real app sends. Includes serial/identity ids (normalised) and timestamps.
Test schema is stricter (NOT NULL) than live for these columns; a local pass implies the live DB also accepts the value.
Known: live flight.services is jsonb ('[]'), local test schema uses text[] ('{}'); the app layer converts. Tracked under the services work, not a bug in the check.
Test schema adds CHECK constraints on enum-like text columns that the Django-era live DB never had; local is stricter, so a local pass implies live accepts the value.
Same CHECK on fuel_type exists on both sides; live wraps it in 'fuel_type IS NULL OR ...' because the column is nullable live, local has it NOT NULL.
Django-era live FKs are DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED with NO ACTION; the test schema uses explicit ON DELETE CASCADE/SET NULL. Delete behaviour differs by design in the test schema.
